subject: Next steps: DPF adoption decision & DPA annex iteration
messages:
From: Tom Reddington <t.reddington@medinsight.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Hughes <emma.hughes@medinsight.com>, MedInsight Legal <legal@medinsight.com>
Date: 2028-01-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: MedInsight: DPF path forward & evidence we still need

Diego — thanks again for last week's walkthrough. We're preparing a recommendation for the data protection board on whether to accept a DPF-based transfer route for EU→US processing for our proofs of concept. Before we lock a path, two asks from legal/compliance: 

1) A short control matrix showing where Redwood's technical/operational controls map to the DPF criteria (encryption, key management, logging, access controls, subprocessors).
2) A draft DPA annex reflecting the nuances of DPF controls (auditing, retention by dataset, cross-border subprocessors list).

Can you confirm if you can deliver both by EOD Wednesday? Also flag any hard constraints — e.g., specific regions where data cannot transit, or limitations on KMS integration with customer-managed keys.

Tom
Head of Privacy, MedInsight

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reddington <t.reddington@medinsight.com>
Cc: Emma Hughes <emma.hughes@medinsight.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-10T11:08:00Z
Subject: Re: MedInsight: DPF path forward & evidence we still need

Tom — thanks, we can take this on. Summary of next steps from our side: 

• I'll attach a control matrix mapping Redwood controls to DPF criteria (technical + organizational).
• Marissa will attach a redline-ready DPA annex (v3) with optional clauses for customer-managed KMS, retention buckets, and audit log retention.
• Laura will confirm the subprocessors list and the timeline for SOC 2 / audit evidence.

Quick notes: 
• Customer-managed keys (CMK) are supported in Redwood Private and Dedicated; for Hosted customers we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS integration via Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) in supported regions — we'll call out which cloud regions enable BYOK. 
• We do not currently perform model training on customer data in hosted mode by default; see annex options for opt-in training usage. 

Deliverables attached. If anything is missing in the matrix, call it out and we'll expand.

Thanks — Diego
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Annex_v3.pdf, crossborder-control-matrix.xlsx, kms_integration_diagram.png

From: Emma Hughes <emma.hughes@medinsight.com>

Cc: Tom Reddington <t.reddington@medinsight.com>, MedInsight Legal <legal@medinsight.com>
Date: 2028-01-11T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: MedInsight: DPF path forward & evidence we still need

Diego/Marissa — received the attachments, thank you. A couple of clarifying questions from legal: 

1) In the control matrix you mark "auditable export logs" — can you confirm retention windows and whether logs can be exported on demand as CSV/PARQUET? We need a mechanism for independent review for our auditors.
2) On subprocessors: we see a host-level CDN provider listed — is there any caching of raw request/response payloads at that layer? If so, what's retained and for how long?

Also: can you provide a short summary of fallback routing if an EU region loses capacity (e.g., will requests failover to US or to another EU region)? That will affect our preferred transfer guardrails.

Emma
Senior Counsel, MedInsight

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Hughes <emma.hughes@medinsight.com>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-12T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: MedInsight: DPF path forward & evidence we still need

Emma — answers inline below. Forwarding excerpts from the annex and control matrix so legal can paste into their RFP response if helpful.

On logs: 
• Retention: Audit/export logs retained by default for 180 days. We offer extended retention add-on (1, 3, 7 years) — see annex clause 4.2.
• Export format: Logs can be exported on demand as CSV or Parquet via the Console (API + UI). We can generate timebound export packages for audits.

On CDN/subprocessor caching: 
• CDN is used for static assets (console UI, telemetry) only. We do not cache request/response model payloads at the CDN. 
• Temporary internal caches (prefix/KV caches) exist in the serving tier to speed token generation — these caches are in-memory and ephemeral; we do not persist full customer payloads to disk. TTLs are short (seconds to minutes) and not replicated off-site.

On routing/failover: 
• Primary policy: region-aware routing. For EU-scoped customer accounts we recommend pinning to an EU region to avoid cross-border routing. 
• Failover behavior: can be configured. Options: 
  - strict: fail requests when EU capacity unavailable (no cross-border failover),
  - permissive: failover to a specified secondary EU region,
  - fallback-to-us: only allowed with customer approval (explicit opt-in).

If you want, we can add a pair of standard fallbacks into the annex (strict + permissive) and leave an opt-in checkbox for fallback-to-us.

Marissa
Senior Product Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Hughes <emma.hughes@medinsight.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reddington <t.reddington@medinsight.com>, MedInsight Legal <legal@medinsight.com>
Date: 2028-01-15T10:30:00Z
Subject: Re: MedInsight: DPF path forward & evidence we still need

Thanks Marissa — that's helpful. Two follow-ups: 

1) Can Redwood provide a signed statement or an export package demonstrating the last 90 days of export logs for a demo tenant (anonymized)? Our audit team wants to validate export mechanics end-to-end.
2) Regarding BYOK in hosted mode: what specific cloud regions currently support BYOK? We need a definitive list to include in our procurement response.

Also, legal reviewed the annex and proposed a minor redline to clause 7 (subprocessor notification timing). They prefer 30 days rather than 60. Can you confirm Redwood's stance?

Emma

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Hughes <emma.hughes@medinsight.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-18T15:04:00Z
Subject: Re: MedInsight: DPF path forward & evidence we still need

Emma — quick status and actions: 

• Export package: we'll prepare an anonymized 90-day export package and a short runbook showing the export process. Delivery ETA: 2028-01-20 EOD. (attachment: dpf-gap-analysis-20280110.docx)
• BYOK regions (hosted): currently supported in eu-west-1, eu-central-1, and eu-north-1. We'll add this table into the annex.
• Subprocessor notice window: we can accept 30 days for customers on enterprise contracts. Standard hosted T&Cs remain 60 days for general customers; we will mark the annex option as "enterprise: 30 days notice".
• Fallback behavior: we will include both the strict and permissive templates in the annex and add an explicit opt-in checkbox for cross-border fallback-to-US.

Next steps: Marissa will issue an updated annex (v3.1) with the BYOK region table, subprocessor notice options, and the fallback templates. I'll share the anonymized export package by 2028-01-20 and copy you when we escalate internal audit evidence (SOC 2 index + auditor point-of-contact).

If that timeline works, I'll send the DocuSign link for the annex once you sign off.

Best — Diego
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
